incident.headline: Gironde fire stabilized but not fixed; no Cap Ferret return signal
incident.summary: The newest reviewed material signal is Le Monde’s 14:11 CEST live update: the 42,000-hectare Gironde fire is described by the interior minister as stabilized but not fixed, and AP separately reports the prefecture saw a globally stable overnight situation with no new evacuations. This is a better fire-behaviour signal than Sunday, but it is not control, containment or reopening. The broader official picture remains severe: nearly 220,000 preventive evacuations in 23 communes, 84 firefighter injuries, major road closures including parts of the A63, and substantial response resources. Cap Ferret remains evacuated and public inbound access is unavailable.

currentAssessment.verdict: The wider Gironde fire is now described as stabilized but not fixed; the Cap Ferret access and no-return position is unchanged.
currentAssessment.narrative: The newest reviewed material signal is Le Monde’s 14:11 CEST live update: the 42,000-hectare Gironde fire is described by Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez as stabilized but not fixed. The Gironde prefecture’s direct 14:00 CEST situation point says the fire did not progress overnight after an eastern flare-up, while still calling the situation unfavorable and describing edge work and tactical firebreaks with aerial support. This improves the fire-behaviour picture after the 12:52 report of fewer active fronts, but it does not mean the fire is controlled or that return is authorized. AP and Le Monde both keep heat and continued firefighting risk in view; the Bordeaux Airport board remains active, and Inforoutes still warns against travel to Saumos, Le Porge, Lège-Cap-Ferret, Arès, Andernos-les-Bains and Marcheprime. For Cap Ferret, the practical conclusion is unchanged: the peninsula remains evacuated, inbound public access is unavailable, road reopening and essential commerce have not been confirmed, and there is no tourist reopening signal.
currentAssessment.confidence: High confidence that the fire-control signal improved but remains short of a return trigger: Le Monde attributes the stabilized/not-fixed status to the interior minister, and the Gironde prefecture directly reports no overnight progression while still calling the situation unfavorable. High confidence that the Cap Ferret practical reopening signal remains negative because evacuation and no-return instructions have not been lifted, Inforoutes continues to warn against travel to the affected sectors, and the mayor’s no-return-until-mastery signal remains operative. High confidence that Bordeaux Airport flight operation remains separate from ground-access risk because the official board continues to list arrivals and departures while publishing separate hotel-zone evacuation and tram-stop disruption notices.

materialUpdates.title: Interior minister says the Gironde fire is stabilized but not fixed
materialUpdates.detail: Le Monde’s 14:11 CEST live update says Emmanuel Macron will visit mobilized forces and elected officials in Gironde, and reports Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez describing the 42,000-hectare Gironde fire as stabilized but not fixed. The Gironde prefecture’s 14:00 CEST situation point directly supports the improved-but-not-safe picture: after a violent flare-up on the eastern side, the fire did not progress overnight, but the situation remains unfavorable and crews are working edges and tactical firebreaks with aerial support. AP separately reports no new evacuations and renewed heat risk. A 14:00 CEST Le Monde Decoders map also reiterates that the fires have been burning since 22 July and remain not fixed; it is visual context rather than an official perimeter or safety instruction.
materialUpdates.incrementalNews: This is a material fire-behaviour improvement after the 12:52 fewer-active-fronts update: the broad Gironde fire is no longer reported as expanding overnight, but the prefecture still describes the situation as unfavorable and the fire is still not fixed or controlled. The same prefecture update adds youth/adapted-stay restrictions during the exceptional fire situation. It does not change Cap Ferret access, no-return instructions, road closures, airport operation, ferries, commerce or reopening signals.

access.name: Travel to the peninsula
access.detail: The entire peninsula remains under an evacuation order. Public inbound travel is not permitted; Lège-Cap-Ferret town hall still says not to return, road access is closed and the partial Arcachon Bay reopening does not create a public maritime route to Cap Ferret.

access.name: Maritime leisure activities
access.detail: Some Arcachon Bay zones far from the fire have reopened, but the peninsula remains evacuated and the maritime-prefecture order keeps the west-coast corridor and embarkation-point safety zones closed.

access.name: Beaches
access.detail: Residents and visitors have been told to leave the area. Municipal lifeguard stations are closed.

access.name: Cycling & hiking
access.detail: All forest cycle paths are closed; Gironde remains at red-level wildfire risk.

localCommerce.name: Groceries and food shops
localCommerce.detail: The evacuation order prevents normal customer access. No general reopening of supermarkets, food shops or the Cap Ferret market has been announced.

localCommerce.name: Pharmacies
localCommerce.detail: No pharmacy-specific reopening or public-access arrangement has been found. Emergency and authority instructions take priority over normal listed hours.

localCommerce.name: Other local shops and services
localCommerce.detail: There is no general announcement that visitor-facing retail or everyday local services have resumed.

ferries.name: Arcachon ↔ Bélisaire ferry
ferries.detail: Arcachon Bay has partly reopened away from the fire, but the west side of the bay and safety circles around Bélisaire, La Vigne, Le Canon, Grand Piquey and Piquey remain restricted. The UBA timetable is not an available public route to the evacuated peninsula.

ferries.name: Emergency evacuation shuttles
ferries.detail: The maritime-prefecture notice says the Union des Bateliers Arcachonnais evacuation boats have been suspended by decision of the Gironde prefect, while embarkation zones are preserved in case maritime evacuation resumes.

ferries.name: Excursions and leisure boats
ferries.status: Partly reopened away from the fire
ferries.detail: Sea users may return only to zones farthest from the fire. Navigation remains prohibited along the west-coast corridor of Arcachon Bay and within safety circles around the evacuation embarkation points.

overall.sourceName: Bordeaux Airport board updated at 15:09 CEST; prefectural evacuation notices

closure.status: Elevated risk · flights operating but heavily disrupted
closure.detail: The official board still lists arrivals and departures, but it flags 3 delayed and 1 cancelled arrivals, plus 0 delayed and 0 cancelled departures. The airport's own flash notice says activity continues, while the hotel zone around the airport is evacuated until further notice and the halls close overnight, so the site cannot provide accommodation. Treat flight operation, terminal overnight access and ground access as separate signals.

groundAccess.status: Disrupted · hotel zone evacuated and airport tram stops skipped
groundAccess.detail: Bordeaux Airport says activity continues and bus/tram services remain provided, but the tram is not stopping between Merignac Soleil and the airport. A separate airport flash notice says the surrounding hotel zone is evacuated by prefectural decision until further notice; because Hall A, Hall B and terminal billi are closed overnight, no accommodation can be provided on the airport site. Travellers are directed to hotels outside evacuated zones or the Parc des Expositions.
